title: Running Total
statement:
Numbers arrive one at a time. After each one, report the total so far.

## Input
The first line contains `n` (1 ≤ n ≤ 10⁵). The second line contains `n` integers, each between −10⁹ and 10⁹.

## Output
Print `n` integers on one line, separated by spaces: the running totals.

title: Digital Root
statement:
Replace a number with the sum of its digits, and repeat until a single digit remains. That digit is the number's digital root.

For example, 9875 becomes 9 + 8 + 7 + 5 = 29, then 2 + 9 = 11, then 1 + 1 = 2.

## Input
The first line contains `t` (1 ≤ t ≤ 1000). Each of the next `t` lines contains a non-negative integer with at most 100 digits.

## Output
For each number, print its digital root on its own line.

title: Mirror Sentence
statement:
A sentence is a **mirror sentence** if its letters read the same forwards and backwards. Ignore case and everything that is not a letter.

`Was it a car or a cat I saw?` is a mirror sentence.

## Input
The first line contains `t` (1 ≤ t ≤ 100). Each of the next `t` lines is a sentence of at most 1000 characters with at least one letter.

## Output
For each sentence print `YES` or `NO`.

title: Second Place
statement:
Given everyone's score, find the second highest **distinct** score. Ties for first place do not count as second place.

## Input
The first line contains `n` (1 ≤ n ≤ 10⁵). The second line contains `n` integers between 0 and 10⁹.

## Output
Print the second highest distinct score, or `NONE` if every score is the same.

tests.explanation: 95 is first. The next distinct score is 88.

title: Clock Hands
statement:
An analog clock shows a time given in 24-hour format. The hour hand moves smoothly: at 3:30 it is halfway between 3 and 4.

Find the smaller angle between the two hands, in degrees.

## Input
The first line contains `t` (1 ≤ t ≤ 1440). Each of the next `t` lines contains a time `HH:MM` with 00 ≤ HH ≤ 23 and 00 ≤ MM ≤ 59.

## Output
For each time print the angle with exactly one digit after the decimal point.

title: Base Hop
statement:
Convert numbers between bases. Digits above 9 use the letters `A` to `Z`, so base 16 uses `0` to `F` and base 36 uses `0` to `Z`.

## Input
The first line contains `t` (1 ≤ t ≤ 1000). Each of the next `t` lines contains `value a b`: a non-negative number written in base `a`, and the base `b` to convert it to (2 ≤ a, b ≤ 36). The value has at most 30 digits and uses uppercase letters.

## Output
For each line print the value written in base `b`, using uppercase letters and no leading zeros.

title: Bit-String Flicking
statement:
Evaluate expressions on bit strings written in **prefix** notation: every operator comes before its operands.

| Operator | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `NOT x` | flip every bit |
| `AND x y`, `OR x y`, `XOR x y` | bitwise, position by position |
| `LSHIFT-k x`, `RSHIFT-k x` | shift by `k` places, filling with zeros |
| `LCIRC-k x`, `RCIRC-k x` | rotate by `k` places, bits wrap around |

All bit strings in one expression have the same length, and results keep that length.

For example `XOR LSHIFT-2 01101 RCIRC-1 10110` is `10100 XOR 01011` which is `11111`.

## Input
The first line contains `t` (1 ≤ t ≤ 500). Each of the next `t` lines is one expression with tokens separated by single spaces. Bit strings have 1 to 16 bits.

## Output
For each expression print the resulting bit string.

title: Postfix Calculator
statement:
In **postfix** notation each operator follows its two operands, so `3 4 + 2 *` means `(3 + 4) * 2`.

Evaluate postfix expressions over integers with the operators `+`, `-`, `*`, `/` and `^`. Division truncates toward zero (so `-7 / 2` is `-3`). `^` raises to a non-negative power.

## Input
The first line contains `t` (1 ≤ t ≤ 1000). Each of the next `t` lines is a valid expression with tokens separated by spaces. Every intermediate value fits in a signed 64-bit integer and no division is by zero.

## Output
For each expression print its value.

title: Bracket Check
statement:
Check whether the brackets `()`, `[]` and `{}` in a line are balanced. Other characters are ignored.

If the line is balanced print `OK`. Otherwise print the 1-based position of the first problem:

- a closing bracket that does not match the most recent unmatched opening bracket, or has none to match, or
- if every closing bracket matched, the leftmost opening bracket that is never closed.

## Input
The first line contains `t` (1 ≤ t ≤ 100). Each of the next `t` lines has at most 10⁵ characters and no spaces.

## Output
For each line print `OK` or a position.

tests.explanation: Line 2 fails at the `]`. Line 3 never closes the first `(`. Line 4 has an extra `}` at position 11.

title: Spiral Order
statement:
Read a grid of numbers in a clockwise spiral: along the top row, down the right column, back along the bottom row, up the left column, then continue inward.

## Input
The first line contains `r` and `c` (1 ≤ r, c ≤ 100). Each of the next `r` lines has `c` integers.

## Output
Print all `r · c` numbers in spiral order on one line, separated by spaces.

title: Prime Gaps
statement:
For each range `[a, b]`, find the largest difference between two **consecutive** primes that both lie in the range. If the range holds fewer than two primes, the answer is `0`.

Between 10 and 30 the primes are 11, 13, 17, 19, 23, 29, so the largest gap is 29 − 23 = 6.

## Input
The first line contains `q` (1 ≤ q ≤ 50). Each of the next `q` lines contains `a` and `b` (1 ≤ a ≤ b ≤ 10⁶).

## Output
For each range print the largest gap.

title: Islands
statement:
A map is a grid of land `#` and water `.`. Land cells that touch horizontally or vertically belong to the same island. Diagonal touching does not count.

Count the islands.

## Input
The first line contains `r` and `c` (1 ≤ r, c ≤ 500). Each of the next `r` lines has `c` characters.

## Output
Print the number of islands.

tests.explanation: Five islands. Cells that touch only at a corner are separate.

title: Knight Distance
statement:
A chess knight moves two squares in one direction and one square perpendicular to it. On an `n × n` board, find the fewest knight moves from one square to another.

## Input
The first line contains `t` (1 ≤ t ≤ 20). Each of the next `t` lines contains `n r1 c1 r2 c2` (1 ≤ n ≤ 300, 1 ≤ r, c ≤ n).

## Output
For each line print the minimum number of moves, or `-1` if the target cannot be reached.

tests.explanation: On a 3 × 3 board the center square is never reachable.

title: Coin Combinations
statement:
Count the ways to pay exactly `x` cents using coins of the given values. You may use any coin as many times as you like, and the order of coins does not matter: `1 + 2` and `2 + 1` are the same way.

The count can be huge, so print it modulo 1 000 000 007.

## Input
The first line contains `n` and `x` (1 ≤ n ≤ 100, 1 ≤ x ≤ 10⁵). The second line contains `n` distinct coin values between 1 and 10⁵.

## Output
Print the number of ways modulo 1 000 000 007.

title: Longest Climb
statement:
A hiker records the altitude at each checkpoint. Find the length of the longest climb: the longest sequence of checkpoints, kept in order but not necessarily adjacent, where each altitude is strictly higher than the one before.

For altitudes `5 2 8 6 3 6 9 7` one longest climb is `2 3 6 9`, so the answer is 4.

## Input
The first line contains `n` (1 ≤ n ≤ 6 · 10⁴). The second line contains `n` integers between 0 and 10⁹.

## Output
Print the length of the longest climb.

An O(n²) solution passes the small tests. The large ones need O(n log n).

title: Room Count
statement:
Each meeting runs from minute `s` up to, but not including, minute `e`. A room can host one meeting at a time, and a meeting ending at minute 30 frees its room for a meeting starting at minute 30.

Find the fewest rooms needed to hold every meeting.

## Input
The first line contains `n` (1 ≤ n ≤ 6 · 10⁴). Each of the next `n` lines contains `s` and `e` (0 ≤ s < e ≤ 10⁹).

## Output
Print the minimum number of rooms.

tests.explanation: Two rooms: one for 0 to 30 then 30 to 40, another for 5 to 10 then 15 to 20.

title: Robot Walk
statement:
A robot starts at `(0, 0)` facing north (the positive `y` direction). It follows a string of commands:

- `F` moves one step forward
- `B` moves one step backward without turning
- `L` turns 90° left
- `R` turns 90° right

Report where it ends up and the farthest it ever got from the start, measured as `|x| + |y|`.

## Input
The first line contains `t` (1 ≤ t ≤ 100). Each of the next `t` lines is a command string of length 1 to 10⁵.

## Output
For each walk print three integers: the final `x`, the final `y`, and the farthest distance reached.

title: Top Words
statement:
Find the `k` most frequent words in a text. A word is a maximal run of letters, compared without case, so `The` and `the` are the same word. Everything that is not a letter separates words.

Sort by count, highest first. Break ties alphabetically.

## Input
The first line contains `k` (1 ≤ k ≤ 50). The rest of the input is the text, at most 10⁵ characters over any number of lines. It has at least `k` distinct words.

## Output
Print `k` lines, each with a word in lowercase and its count.
